verses.1: And Joseph came and reported to Pharaoh, saying, “My father, my brothers, and their families, and all those who belong to them, have come from Canaan. They are now in a foreign land.”
verses.2: And from among his brothers, he took five men and brought them before Pharaoh.
verses.3: And Pharaoh said to his brothers, “What are you doing?” They replied, “We too are your servants. Our fathers too are your servants.”
verses.4: And they said to Pharaoh, “Let us go into the land. There is no food to feed your servants here. It’s better for us to starve in the land of Canaan. Now, please let your servants live in the land of Goshen.”
verses.5: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.”
verses.6: The land of Egypt is before you. It’s a good land, where your father and your brothers will be able to live. But if you know that there are people living there, and they are rulers who rule over those lands…
verses.7: And Joseph brought his father Jacob before Pharaoh. He stood before Pharaoh and blessed Jacob.
verses.8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many days are there left in your life?”
verses.9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, “During the days of my two years of wandering, it was very difficult. Those were difficult times for me. I failed to live up to the standards set by my ancestors during their time of wandering.”
verses.10: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and then he left before Pharaoh.
verses.11: And Josue placed his father and his brothers in charge of the land of Egypt. He gave them possession of the land, the land of Raamses, as Pharaoh commanded.
verses.12: And Joseph ate his father and his brothers, along with all the family of his father, as food, according to the commandment.
verses.13: And there is no bread in all the land; there is extreme hunger. The land of Egypt and the land of Canaan were destroyed because of this hunger.
verses.14: And Joseph took all the money that was found in Egypt and in Canaan. He brought the money back to Pharaoh’s house.
verses.15: And the money was taken from Egypt and from Canaan. All the people of Egypt went to Joseph, saying, “Give us some bread, for we are starving, and why have you lost our money?”
verses.16: And Joseph said, “Take your money from your homes, and give it to me in your own homes. But if there’s no money available, then I will give you something else instead.”
verses.17: And they brought their offerings to Joseph. Joseph gave them bread from the donkeys, as well as food from their own stores. He also distributed it among all the people during that year.
verses.18: And that year passed away. In the second year, they came to him and said, “We will not leave our fields and livestock with Adoni. We will not stay before Adoni unless our land and our property are returned to us.”
verses.19: Why have we become like dead bodies in your eyes? We and our land will be given to Pharaoh as slaves. He will give us seed, and we will live, and we will not die. And the land will not be lost.
verses.20: And Josiah gathered all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, because the people of Egypt had sold their fields to others. The famine became severe among them, and the land became Pharaoh’s.
verses.21: And he brought the people to cities on both sides of the borders of Egypt, from one end to the other.
verses.22: Only the land belonging to the priests was not sold. This was because there was a law regarding the priests: they were required to follow the laws given to them by Pharaoh. Therefore, they did not sell their land.
verses.23: And Joseph said to the people, “Today I have bought you and your land from Pharaoh. Now, you may plant seeds on this land.”
verses.24: And there will be five fingers for you to use as seeds for the fields. The other four fingers will be used for your food, for those who live in your households, and for your own consumption.
verses.25: And they said, “Our lives are found to be pleasing in the eyes of Adonai. Thus, we will be servants of Pharaoh.”
verses.26: And Joseph placed it as a sign on the land of Egypt, for Pharaoh’s sake. Only the land belonging to the priests was not given to Pharaoh.
verses.27: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in a land full of hardships. They were trapped there, and they multiplied and grew in number.
verses.28: Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for twenty-five years. Those were two decades and forty years of Jacob’s life.
verses.29: And the days of Israel approached their destruction. They called for Josue to come to them. They said to him, “If you find favor in your eyes, please put your hand under my feet. Then you will show me kindness and truthfulness. Please do not bury me in Egypt.”
verses.30: And I lay down with my fathers, and they raised me up from Egypt. They buried me in their tomb. And He said, “I will do as you say.”
verses.31: And he said, “May seventy be given to me.” And so they gave him seventy. Then Israel bowed down before the head of the mitzvah.
